advice-after-class: Mia has a sore throat, so she asks Leo to lead the group rehearsal. Leo suggests moving it to the library. If the library is full, the group will use Room 8.
quieter-classroom: Our group will try a quiet start on Monday. If it works, we'll do it again on Thursday. Students can still ask for help, but they'll write their questions down first.
school-day-fixes: Nina keeps forgetting the group materials. Her friend tells her to put them by the front door at night. If Nina remembers them all week, she'll stop using the reminder on Sunday.
tried-it-once: I have tried rock climbing once. I went with my cousin last May. I liked the climbing, but I haven't been back because the gym is far from my house.
day-by-the-lake: I'd take a camera if we spent a day at the lake. Anna would rather go to the stream because she likes to watch birds there. We'd both bring food from home.
new-hobby-challenge: Sam signed up for a nature photography challenge last Friday. He's never taken a photo of a wild animal. If he had a better camera, he'd try to photograph the birds at sunrise.
which-form-fits: Pablo has never given a talk in English. He gets nervous in front of a crowd, so his partner tells him to practice with two friends first. If that goes well, he'll practice with the whole group on Friday.
my-next-challenge: I've already tried drawing, so this month I'm going to take up running. I'll start with short runs after school. If it rains on Tuesday, I'll go on Wednesday instead.
what-would-you-do: If I could choose any place for our class outing, I'd choose the waterfall. I went there last year. The walk was easy, but I'd tell everyone to wear boots because the path can get muddy.
listen-for-the-change: The group was going to meet at nine on the shore. The weather looks bad, so they'll meet at ten at the visitor center instead. If the weather improves, they will walk to the stream later.
before-you-choose: The class can spend Friday at the sports center or the nature reserve. The reserve is cheaper, but the trip takes an hour. Daniela has already been to the sports center, so she'd prefer the reserve.
two-replies: My first choice was the art club, but it's full. If the school opens a second group, I'll join. I've never tried chess, so I might go to the chess club while I wait.
pitch-a-small-change: Our team asked twelve students about the amount of paper we use. Eight of them wanted a box for paper they could use again. If the school agrees, we'll put one box beside the printer and check it after a week.
busy-week-at-work: Our team has three deadlines this week. Sara says the payroll file comes first because it's due at noon. She'll ask Luis to check the stock report while she finishes it.
move-the-deadline: Hi Ava, our supplier hasn't sent the last two prices. The budget was due on Tuesday. I'm asking Mr. Ruiz if we can hand it in by Thursday morning instead.
better-shift-plan: People on the morning shift get several calls at once. Elena suggests that one person answer calls and the other check stock. She wants to try the new plan for a week before asking the manager to approve it.
missing-order: A customer called because her order hadn't arrived. We checked the system and found that the street number was wrong. We corrected the address and sent a new package the next morning.
what-could-go-wrong: The supplier can send the boxes on Friday. Rosa is worried because the fair starts on Friday morning. She suggests calling a local supplier today to ask about a backup order.
wrong-invoice: Our invoice says we bought thirty folders, but the delivery note says twenty. Paula will compare both documents with the original purchase order. She'll email the supplier if the order also says twenty.
read-the-office-note: I received invoice 061 on Monday. It includes a delivery charge that wasn't in the quotation. I'll call the supplier, then send a short email asking them to confirm the total in writing.
which-supplier-works: Pack Right charges sixty dollars and can deliver on Monday. Quick Box charges seventy-five and can deliver on Thursday. We need recycled boxes by Friday. Only Quick Box sells recycled boxes, and we can spend up to eighty dollars.
clear-follow-up: At yesterday's meeting we agreed to check the figures before contacting the client. Marta will confirm the price today. I'll send the final quotation tomorrow morning.
check-the-totals: The report puts office supplies at forty-eight dollars. We found one receipt for thirty dollars and another for twelve. Before I change the report, I'll ask the buyer if there's a third receipt.
client-needs-an-answer: A client asked if the new price includes delivery. It does, but the quotation is only valid until Wednesday. I will send a reply this afternoon and attach the updated quotation.
payment-reminder: Invoice eighty-four was due last Tuesday. The client says their payment went through on Thursday. We haven't seen it yet, so I'll ask them to send a copy of the transfer receipt.
explain-the-budget: Our project budget is one hundred dollars. We plan to spend sixty on materials and twenty on printing. That leaves twenty for unexpected costs. If the printing gets more expensive, we'll print fewer copies.
